grammarName.en: Future continuous · be about to · timetables
grammarName.ru: Future continuous · be about to · расписания

scenario: Valery, who has said 'I'm retiring on Friday' for years, is FINALLY retiring for real — a warm payoff to the running joke. The team throws a small farewell, so the episode is full of future continuous, 'be about to', and present simple for timetables. Kate says, 'This time next week, Valery will be relaxing at home, not fixing bugs.' Pol adds, 'He'll be collecting his stamps every morning.' The party is planned with timetables: 'The cake arrives at four. The speeches start at five.' Alex checks the clock: 'Kate is about to give a speech!' Valery is quietly happy: 'This time tomorrow, I won't be setting an alarm.' Peter asks what he will be doing next year. Everyone is a little sad but mostly happy. Use clear future continuous ('will be + -ing' for actions in progress at a future time), 'be about to + verb' for the very near future, and present simple for the timetable. Short B1 sentences; keep the warm, gentle tone.
